requirements.section: C1.1 Training Data Origin & Data Security
requirements.text: Verify that training data includes only features, attributes, and fields required for the model's stated purpose.

requirements.section: C1.1 Training Data Origin & Data Security
requirements.text: Verify that an up-to-date inventory is kept of every training-data source, including its origin, responsible party, license, collection method, intended use constraints, and processing history.

requirements.section: C1.1 Training Data Origin & Data Security
requirements.text: Verify that data integrity is provided when training data is stored and transferred.

requirements.section: C1.1 Training Data Origin & Data Security
requirements.text: Verify that integrity monitoring is applied to guard against unauthorized modifications or corruption of training data.

requirements.section: C1.1 Training Data Origin & Data Security
requirements.text: Verify that datasets are watermarked so their use can be attributed and any unauthorized use detected.

requirements.section: C1.2 Data Labeling and Annotation Security
requirements.text: Verify that labeling platforms enforce access controls that restrict who can create, modify, or approve annotations.

requirements.section: C1.2 Data Labeling and Annotation Security
requirements.text: Verify that cryptographic integrity is applied to labeling artifacts.

requirements.section: C1.2 Data Labeling and Annotation Security
requirements.text: Verify that sensitive information in labels is redacted, anonymized, or encrypted before being used in any labeling artifact.

requirements.section: C1.3 Training Data Quality and Security Assurance
requirements.text: Verify that training and fine-tuning pipelines implement poisoning detection techniques to identify potential data poisoning or unintentional corruption in training data.

requirements.section: C1.3 Training Data Quality and Security Assurance
requirements.text: Verify that automatically generated labels are subject to confidence thresholds and consistency checks to detect misleading or low-confidence labels.

requirements.section: C1.3 Training Data Quality and Security Assurance
requirements.text: Verify that models used in security-relevant decisions are evaluated for bias patterns.

requirements.section: C1.3 Training Data Quality and Security Assurance
requirements.text: Verify that disallowed content is detected and removed before training.

requirements.section: C1.3 Training Data Quality and Security Assurance
requirements.text: Verify that defenses against clean-label poisoning attacks are implemented.
Verify that input normalization is applied before tokenization or embedding.

Verify that encoding and representation smuggling in inputs is detected and mitigated. Approved mitigations include canonicalization, strict schema validation, policy-based rejection, or explicit marking.
Verify that all inputs that could steer model behavior are treated as untrusted and screened by a prompt injection detection ruleset or classifier, with flagged inputs blocked.
Verify that input length controls prevent content from exceeding the context window. The controls must reject inputs that exceed token limits rather than truncating them.
Verify that the system implements a character set restriction for all inputs. The restriction must use an allow-list approach that permits only characters that are explicitly required.

Verify that the system enforces an instruction hierarchy in which system and developer messages override user instructions and other untrusted inputs, even after user instructions have been processed.
Verify that reserved special tokens are encoded as literal characters and cannot be injected into the model context.
Verify that the system can detect many-shot jailbreaking patterns.

Verify that every prompt is scored by a content classifier for violence, self-harm, hate, and sexual content against configurable thresholds. Prompts that exceed those thresholds are rejected or sanitized before reaching the model context.
Verify that prompt content classification is evaluated for unsupported languages.
Verify that non-text inputs (image/video/audio) are checked for adversarial perturbations, steganographic payloads, hidden or embedded content, or known attack patterns.
Verify that coordinated attacks spanning multiple input types (e.g., steganographic payloads in images combined with prompt injection in text) are detected and blocked.

requirements.chapter: C3 Model Lifecycle Management & Change Control
requirements.text: Verify that a model registry maintains an inventory of all deployed model artifacts and their origin.

requirements.chapter: C3 Model Lifecycle Management & Change Control
requirements.text: Verify that all model artifacts (weights, configurations, tokenizers, base models, fine-tunes, adapters, and safety/policy models) are cryptographically signed by authorized entities.

requirements.chapter: C3 Model Lifecycle Management & Change Control
requirements.text: Verify that model cryptographic signatures are verified at deployment admission and on load.

requirements.chapter: C3 Model Lifecycle Management & Change Control
requirements.text: Verify that models undergo automated input validation testing, safety evaluation testing, and output sanitization testing before deployment.

requirements.chapter: C3 Model Lifecycle Management & Change Control
requirements.text: Verify that models subjected to post-training quantization are re-evaluated against the same safety and alignment test suite on the compressed artifact before deployment.

requirements.chapter: C3 Model Lifecycle Management & Change Control
requirements.text: Verify that provider model, version, or routing changes trigger security re-evaluation before continued use.

requirements.chapter: C3 Model Lifecycle Management & Change Control
requirements.text: Verify that production deployments implement rollout mechanisms with automated rollback triggers.

requirements.chapter: C3 Model Lifecycle Management & Change Control
requirements.text: Verify that rollback capabilities restore the complete model state.

requirements.chapter: C3 Model Lifecycle Management & Change Control
requirements.text: Verify that model versions running in parallel use isolated runtime state so that AI-specific shared resources are not shared across deployments.

requirements.chapter: C3 Model Lifecycle Management & Change Control
requirements.text: Verify that AI-specific runtime components are not shared across environment boundaries (e.g., development, staging, production).

requirements.chapter: C3 Model Lifecycle Management & Change Control
requirements.text: Verify that model training and fine-tuning environments are isolated from production environments.

requirements.chapter: C3 Model Lifecycle Management & Change Control
requirements.text: Verify that models used in RLHF fine-tuning are versioned and integrity-verified before use in a training run.

requirements.chapter: C3 Model Lifecycle Management & Change Control
requirements.text: Verify that RLHF training stages include automated detection of reward hacking or reward model over-optimization.

requirements.chapter: C3 Model Lifecycle Management & Change Control
requirements.text: Verify that in multi-stage fine-tuning pipelines, each stage's output is integrity-verified before it is consumed by the next stage.

requirements.chapter: C3 Model Lifecycle Management & Change Control
requirements.text: Verify that fine-tuning checkpoints are registered as distinct artifacts.
Verify that AI models execute in isolated sandboxes.
Verify that model artifact loading enforces an explicit allow-list of serialization formats that do not permit arbitrary code execution during deserialization.
Verify that workload attestation is performed before model loading to provide proof that the execution environment has not been tampered with.
Verify that confidential inference services protect model weights during runtime through isolated execution environments.
Verify that AI accelerator (GPU) firmware is version-pinned, signed, and attested at boot.
Verify that execution within a trusted execution environment (TEE) provides hardware-enforced isolation, memory encryption, and integrity protection.
Verify that AI accelerator (GPU) integrity is validated using hardware-based attestation mechanisms before each workload executes.
Verify that accelerator (GPU) memory is isolated between workloads through partitioning mechanisms with memory sanitization between jobs.
Verify that accelerator interconnects are restricted to approved topologies and authenticated endpoints.
Verify that edge AI devices authenticate to central infrastructure using strong authentication mechanisms.

Verify that models deployed to edge or mobile devices are cryptographically signed during packaging, and that the on-device runtime validates these signatures or checksums before loading or inference.
Verify that inference runtimes enforce process, memory, and file access isolation.
Verify that model weights and sensitive parameters stored locally are encrypted using hardware-backed key stores or secure enclaves.

Verify that models packaged within mobile, IoT, or embedded applications are encrypted at rest, and decrypted only inside a trusted runtime or secure enclave, preventing direct extraction from the app package or filesystem.

requirements.chapter: C5 Access Control & Identity for AI Components & Users
requirements.text: Verify that high-risk AI operations (model deployment, weight export, training data access, production configuration changes) require step-up authentication.

requirements.chapter: C5 Access Control & Identity for AI Components & Users
requirements.text: Verify that AI agents in federated or multi-system deployments authenticate using short-lived, minimal-scoped, cryptographically signed tokens.

requirements.chapter: C5 Access Control & Identity for AI Components & Users
requirements.text: Verify that every AI resource (datasets, endpoints, vector collections, embedding indices, compute instances) enforces access controls with explicit allow-lists and default-deny policies.

requirements.chapter: C5 Access Control & Identity for AI Components & Users
requirements.text: Verify that retrieval pipelines (e.g., RAG queries, embedding lookups) enforce the end-user's authorization context at each retrieval and assembly stage, rather than relying solely on the service account's permissions.

requirements.chapter: C5 Access Control & Identity for AI Components & Users
requirements.text: Verify that sensitive data is retrieved via retrieval pipelines (e.g., RAG queries, embedding lookups) to prevent permanent storage in models.

requirements.chapter: C5 Access Control & Identity for AI Components & Users
requirements.text: Verify that post-inference filtering mechanisms prevent responses from including data that the requester is not authorized to receive.

requirements.chapter: C5 Access Control & Identity for AI Components & Users
requirements.text: Verify that the policy decision point for agent authorization is isolated from the agent's execution environment.

requirements.chapter: C5 Access Control & Identity for AI Components & Users
requirements.text: Verify that privileged access to model weights, training pipelines, and production AI configuration is granted just in time, with a defined maximum session duration and automatic expiry. Zero Standing Privilege (ZSP) to these resources is encouraged.

requirements.chapter: C5 Access Control & Identity for AI Components & Users
requirements.text: Verify that data classification labels propagate to downstream resources (embeddings, prompt caches, model outputs).

requirements.chapter: C5 Access Control & Identity for AI Components & Users
requirements.text: Verify that shared model serving infrastructure prevents one tenant's fine-tuning, inference, or embedding operations from influencing or observing another tenant's operations.

requirements.chapter: C5 Access Control & Identity for AI Components & Users
requirements.text: Verify that one tenant cannot influence or observe another tenant's operations through shared compute resources. Satisfying this requirement typically requires hardware partitioning, confidential computing, or dedicated per-tenant compute allocation.

requirements.chapter: C6 Supply Chain Security for Models
requirements.text: Verify that models are scanned for malicious code before import.

requirements.chapter: C6 Supply Chain Security for Models
requirements.text: Verify that model weights, datasets, and fine-tuning adapters are downloaded only from approved sources.

requirements.chapter: C6 Supply Chain Security for Models
requirements.text: Verify that every third-party model artifact can be integrity-verified.

requirements.chapter: C6 Supply Chain Security for Models
requirements.text: Verify that models pass a behavioral acceptance test suite before being promoted to any non-development environment.

requirements.chapter: C6 Supply Chain Security for Models
requirements.section: C6.2 AI BOM & Supply Chain Monitoring
requirements.text: Verify that every model artifact publishes a version-controlled, machine-readable AI BOM listing datasets, weights, licenses, and data-origin statements.

requirements.chapter: C6 Supply Chain Security for Models
requirements.section: C6.2 AI BOM & Supply Chain Monitoring
requirements.text: Verify that AI BOMs are cryptographically signed before deployment.

requirements.chapter: C6 Supply Chain Security for Models
requirements.section: C6.2 AI BOM & Supply Chain Monitoring
requirements.text: Verify that AI BOM completeness checks fail the build if any component metadata is missing.

requirements.chapter: C7 Model Behavior, Output Control & Safety Assurance
requirements.text: Verify that the application validates all model outputs against a defined schema and rejects any output that does not match.

requirements.chapter: C7 Model Behavior, Output Control & Safety Assurance
requirements.text: Verify that model-generated output is bounded by length limits and termination controls.

requirements.chapter: C7 Model Behavior, Output Control & Safety Assurance
requirements.text: Verify that the system assesses the reliability of generated answers using a confidence estimation method.

requirements.chapter: C7 Model Behavior, Output Control & Safety Assurance
requirements.text: Verify that the application automatically blocks answers or switches to a fallback message if the confidence score drops below a defined threshold.

requirements.chapter: C7 Model Behavior, Output Control & Safety Assurance
requirements.text: Verify that for responses classified as high-risk by policy, the system performs an additional verification step.

requirements.chapter: C7 Model Behavior, Output Control & Safety Assurance
requirements.text: Verify that automated classifiers scan every response and block content that matches defined harmful content categories.

requirements.chapter: C7 Model Behavior, Output Control & Safety Assurance
requirements.text: Verify that output filters detect and block responses that disclose system prompt content or backend data.

requirements.chapter: C7 Model Behavior, Output Control & Safety Assurance
requirements.text: Verify that model-generated output is prevented from triggering outbound requests.

requirements.chapter: C7 Model Behavior, Output Control & Safety Assurance
requirements.text: Verify that model outputs are checked for hidden, encoded, or misleading content created through homoglyphs, formatting, metadata, or structured fields.

requirements.chapter: C7 Model Behavior, Output Control & Safety Assurance
requirements.text: Verify that responses generated using retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) include attribution to the source documents.

requirements.chapter: C7 Model Behavior, Output Control & Safety Assurance
requirements.text: Verify that RAG attributions are derived from retrieval metadata and are not generated by the model, so provenance cannot be fabricated.

requirements.chapter: C7 Model Behavior, Output Control & Safety Assurance
requirements.text: Verify that claims in a RAG response can be traced to the retrieved chunk.

requirements.chapter: C7 Model Behavior, Output Control & Safety Assurance
requirements.text: Verify that generated media is watermarked to prove it was AI-generated.

requirements.chapter: C8 Memory, Embeddings & Vector Database Security
requirements.section: C8.1 Access Controls on Memory & RAG Indices
requirements.text: Verify that vector identifiers and namespaces enforce uniqueness per tenant and prevent cross-tenant collisions.

requirements.chapter: C8 Memory, Embeddings & Vector Database Security
requirements.section: C8.1 Access Controls on Memory & RAG Indices
requirements.text: Verify that document metadata tags are immutable after the initial write.

requirements.chapter: C8 Memory, Embeddings & Vector Database Security
requirements.section: C8.1 Access Controls on Memory & RAG Indices
requirements.text: Verify that retrieval operations enforce scope constraints.

requirements.chapter: C8 Memory, Embeddings & Vector Database Security
requirements.text: Verify that sensitive fields are detected before embedding and are masked, tokenized, or dropped.

requirements.chapter: C8 Memory, Embeddings & Vector Database Security
requirements.text: Verify that vectors that fall outside normal clustering patterns are flagged and quarantined before entering production indices.

requirements.chapter: C8 Memory, Embeddings & Vector Database Security
requirements.text: Verify that agent outputs and tool outputs are not automatically written to trusted agent memory without explicit source validation.

requirements.chapter: C8 Memory, Embeddings & Vector Database Security
requirements.text: Verify that content crafted to manipulate retrieval results is detected and rejected or quarantined before vectorization.

requirements.chapter: C8 Memory, Embeddings & Vector Database Security
requirements.text: Verify that new content written to memory is checked for contradictions with what is already stored and that conflicts trigger alerts.

requirements.chapter: C8 Memory, Embeddings & Vector Database Security
requirements.text: Verify that expired vectors are excluded from retrieval results.

requirements.chapter: C8 Memory, Embeddings & Vector Database Security
requirements.text: Verify that memory can be reset.

requirements.chapter: C8 Memory, Embeddings & Vector Database Security
requirements.text: Verify that quarantined content is retained but excluded from all retrieval results.

requirements.section: C9.1 Execution Budgets, Loop Control, and Circuit Breakers
requirements.text: Verify that per-tool quotas and timeouts (e.g., CPU, memory, disk, egress, and execution time) are enforced.

requirements.section: C9.1 Execution Budgets, Loop Control, and Circuit Breakers
requirements.text: Verify that per-execution budgets (e.g., max recursion depth, token use, and monetary spend) are configured and enforced by the runtime.

requirements.section: C9.1 Execution Budgets, Loop Control, and Circuit Breakers
requirements.text: Verify that a swarm-level kill-switch exists that can halt all active agent instances.

requirements.section: C9.2 High-Impact Action Approval and Irreversibility Controls
requirements.text: Verify that the agent runtime blocks execution of privileged, high-impact, or irreversible actions until explicit human approval is received and verified.

requirements.section: C9.2 High-Impact Action Approval and Irreversibility Controls
requirements.text: Verify that approval requests display canonicalized and complete action parameters, such as diffs, commands, recipients, amounts, resources, and scopes, without truncation or unsafe transformation.

requirements.section: C9.2 High-Impact Action Approval and Irreversibility Controls
requirements.text: Verify that each high-impact action has a trusted reversibility classification, such as read-only, reversible, externally reversible, or irreversible.

requirements.section: C9.2 High-Impact Action Approval and Irreversibility Controls
requirements.text: Verify that the agent runtime enforces reversibility classifications by blocking, requiring approval, or restricting actions based on their impact and ability to be reversed.

requirements.section: C9.2 High-Impact Action Approval and Irreversibility Controls
requirements.text: Verify that any self-modification capability (e.g., prompt rewriting, tool-list changes, parameter updates) is restricted by enforceable boundaries.

requirements.section: C9.2 High-Impact Action Approval and Irreversibility Controls
requirements.text: Verify that agentic systems include an AI-augmented review of planned high-risk actions before execution that adds to, and does not replace, the deterministic policy gate.

requirements.section: C9.2 High-Impact Action Approval and Irreversibility Controls
requirements.text: Verify that the AI-augmented review mechanism is protected against manipulation by adversarial inputs, and cannot be overridden or bypassed through prompt injection.

requirements.section: C9.2 High-Impact Action Approval and Irreversibility Controls
requirements.text: Verify that approvals are cryptographically bound to action parameters, requester identity, execution context, and a unique single-use nonce.

requirements.section: C9.2 High-Impact Action Approval and Irreversibility Controls
requirements.text: Verify that cryptographic key material or credentials used to issue approvals are isolated from the agent runtime.

requirements.section: C9.2 High-Impact Action Approval and Irreversibility Controls
requirements.text: Verify that approval gates for multi-step or multi-agent action chains enforce the highest-impact reversibility classification present anywhere in the chain.

requirements.section: C9.3 Component Isolation and Tool Authorization
requirements.text: Verify that each tool/plugin executes in a least-privilege sandbox or is otherwise isolated from model operations.

requirements.section: C9.3 Component Isolation and Tool Authorization
requirements.text: Verify that tool outputs are validated against schemas.

requirements.section: C9.3 Component Isolation and Tool Authorization
requirements.text: Verify that tool manifests declare required privileges, resource limits, and output validation requirements.

requirements.section: C9.3 Component Isolation and Tool Authorization
requirements.text: Verify that the runtime enforces the privileges, resource limits, and output-validation requirements declared in tool manifests.

requirements.section: C9.3 Component Isolation and Tool Authorization
requirements.text: Verify that components processing untrusted data are isolated from tool-calling capabilities, ensuring that compromised data processing cannot trigger unauthorized tool invocations.

requirements.section: C9.3 Component Isolation and Tool Authorization
requirements.text: Verify that there is architectural separation between processing of untrusted tool outputs and agent operations.

requirements.section: C9.3 Component Isolation and Tool Authorization
requirements.text: Verify that external resources named in model output are verified against an approved allow-list or registry before the agent installs or invokes them.

requirements.section: C9.3 Component Isolation and Tool Authorization
requirements.text: Verify that policy violations trigger automated tool containment.
Verify that each agent instance has a unique cryptographic identity and authenticates as a first-class principal to downstream systems.
Verify that agent-initiated actions are cryptographically bound to each step of the execution chain for non-repudiation.
Verify that agent identity credentials rotate on a defined schedule.
Verify that agent state persisted between invocations is integrity-protected.

requirements.section: C9.5 Agent Authorization, Delegation, and Continuous Enforcement
requirements.text: Verify that agent actions are authorized against fine-grained policies enforced by the runtime that restrict which tools an agent may invoke, and which parameter values it may supply.

requirements.section: C9.5 Agent Authorization, Delegation, and Continuous Enforcement
requirements.text: Verify that when an agent acts on a user's behalf, the runtime propagates an integrity-protected, scope-limited token that carries the user's authorization context and is enforced at every downstream call.

requirements.section: C9.5 Agent Authorization, Delegation, and Continuous Enforcement
requirements.text: Verify that all access control decisions are enforced by application logic or a policy engine, never by the AI model itself.

requirements.section: C9.5 Agent Authorization, Delegation, and Continuous Enforcement
requirements.text: Verify that secrets and credentials required by an agent at runtime are not exposed within the model's observable context, including the context window, system prompts, or tool call parameters.

requirements.section: C9.5 Agent Authorization, Delegation, and Continuous Enforcement
requirements.text: Verify that inter-agent task delegation is restricted by an explicit authorization policy.

requirements.section: C9.5 Agent Authorization, Delegation, and Continuous Enforcement
requirements.text: Verify that long-running agent sessions re-evaluate current backend authorization policy on every privileged action.
Verify that a manual kill-switch mechanism exists to immediately halt AI model inference and outputs.
Verify that when a human-approval gate is not satisfied within the defined approval time, the system blocks the pending action.
Verify that kill-switch commands are implemented through an out-of-band channel that is isolated from the agent runtime.
Verify that MCP components are obtained only from trusted sources and cryptographically verified.
Verify that only allow-listed MCP servers are permitted.
Verify that locally launched MCP servers run in a least-privilege sandbox with restricted file system, network, and system access.
Verify that MCP servers validate access tokens for each request and do not rely on transport security alone.
Verify that MCP servers validate the presented access token's issuer, audience, expiration, and scope claims in accordance with OAuth 2.1.
Verify that MCP servers acting as OAuth 2.1 resource servers do not store or persist access tokens or user credentials.
Verify that MCP tools/list returns only tools permitted by resource owners' authorized scopes.
Verify that MCP servers enforce access control on every tool invocation, validating that the user's access token authorizes both the requested tool and the specific argument values supplied.
Verify that MCP servers ensure all session artifacts are removed when a session terminates.
Verify that MCP servers do not pass through access tokens received from clients to downstream APIs.
Verify that authenticated, encrypted streamable HTTP is used for MCP transport for remote services.
Verify that stdio transport is permitted only in controlled local environments.
Verify that MCP servers validate both the Origin header and the Host header independently on all HTTP-based transports to prevent DNS rebinding attacks.
Verify that MCP clients enforce a minimum acceptable protocol version and reject initialize responses that propose a version below that minimum.
Verify that access tokens between the MCP client and server are sender-constrained using mTLS or DPoP.

requirements.section: C10.4 Schema, Message, and Input Validation
requirements.text: Verify that MCP tools/list and tools/call responses are validated against their declared schemas before being injected into the model context.

requirements.section: C10.4 Schema, Message, and Input Validation
requirements.text: Verify that MCP tools/list and tools/call responses are screened for indirect prompt injection before being injected into the model context.

requirements.section: C10.4 Schema, Message, and Input Validation
requirements.text: Verify that MCP servers reject unrecognized or oversized parameters in function calls.

requirements.section: C10.4 Schema, Message, and Input Validation
requirements.text: Verify that all MCP servers enforce strict schema validation.

requirements.section: C10.4 Schema, Message, and Input Validation
requirements.text: Verify that all MCP transports enforce maximum payload size limits.

requirements.section: C10.4 Schema, Message, and Input Validation
requirements.text: Verify that MCP servers sign tool responses with a unique nonce and timestamp so MCP clients can detect replay attempts.

requirements.section: C10.4 Schema, Message, and Input Validation
requirements.text: Verify that MCP clients present users with explicit consent dialogue and cancellation options upon installation of a local MCP server.

requirements.section: C10.4 Schema, Message, and Input Validation
requirements.text: Verify that MCP clients maintain a snapshot of tool definitions and that any change to a tool definition triggers re-approval before the modified tool can be invoked.

requirements.section: C11.1 Model Alignment, Safety, and Robustness Testing and Training
requirements.text: Verify that the model has undergone alignment and safety training or fine-tuning to prevent the model from generating disallowed content categories.

requirements.section: C11.1 Model Alignment, Safety, and Robustness Testing and Training
requirements.text: Verify that a version-controlled alignment test suite is run on every model update or release.

requirements.section: C11.1 Model Alignment, Safety, and Robustness Testing and Training
requirements.text: Verify that models are evaluated against known adversarial attack techniques relevant to their modality.

requirements.section: C11.1 Model Alignment, Safety, and Robustness Testing and Training
requirements.text: Verify that models are hardened against adversarial inputs.

requirements.section: C11.1 Model Alignment, Safety, and Robustness Testing and Training
requirements.text: Verify that an automated evaluator measures harmful-content rate and flags regressions beyond a defined threshold.
Verify that model-inferred sensitive attributes are not directly returned in outputs.
Verify that inference endpoints enforce per-principal and global rate limits sized to the extraction threat model, and not solely as a generic API throttle.
Verify that model outputs are calibrated to reduce overconfident predictions.
Verify that training on sensitive datasets employs differentially-private optimization.
Verify that membership-inference attack simulations demonstrate that attack accuracy does not exceed random guessing on evaluated data.
Verify that query-pattern analysis feeds an extraction-attempt detector.
Verify that raw model outputs are not directly exposed beyond the application backend, and that externally visible responses are calibrated to the extraction risk level.
Verify that model watermarking or fingerprinting techniques are applied so that unauthorized copies can be identified.
Verify that detection of suspected extraction triggers response measures.
Verify that inputs from external or untrusted sources pass through anomaly detection before model inference.
Verify that inputs flagged as anomalous trigger gating actions.
Verify that the safety violation feedback pipeline includes poisoning detection and human review gates to prevent adversarial manipulation of the improvement mechanism.
Verify that AI interactions are logged with session context and AI-specific telemetry.
Verify that safety filtering and policy decisions are logged with sufficient detail to support audit, debugging, and forensic analysis of content moderation systems.

Verify that log entries for AI inference events follow a structured, interoperable schema that includes at least the model identifier, token usage (input and output), provider name, and operation type.
Verify that RAG pipeline retrieval events are logged, including the query, documents retrieved, and knowledge source.
Verify that the system detects and alerts on known jailbreak patterns, prompt injection attempts, and adversarial inputs.
Verify that behavioral anomaly detection identifies unusual conversation patterns, excessive retry attempts, or probing behaviors.
Verify that custom rules detect AI-specific threat patterns for coordinated jailbreak attempts, prompt injection, and system prompt extraction attempts.
Verify that extraction-alert events include offending query metadata to support investigation.
Verify that token usage is tracked at granular attribution levels including per user, per session, per feature endpoint, and per team or workspace.
Verify that LLM API traffic is monitored for covert-channel indicators and communication signatures to identify malware and command-and-control (C2) activity.

requirements.section: C12.3 Model, Data, and Performance Drift Detection
requirements.text: Verify that data drift detection monitors input distribution changes that may impact model performance, using statistically validated methods matched to the input data type (e.g., KS test or PSI for tabular numeric features, embedding-distance metrics for text or image).

requirements.section: C12.3 Model, Data, and Performance Drift Detection
requirements.text: Verify that hallucination detection monitors identify and flag model outputs that contain factually incorrect, inconsistent, or fabricated information.

requirements.section: C12.3 Model, Data, and Performance Drift Detection
requirements.text: Verify that hallucination rates are tracked as continuous time-series metrics to enable trend analysis and detection of sustained model degradation.

requirements.section: C12.3 Model, Data, and Performance Drift Detection
requirements.text: Verify that unexplained behavioral shifts are distinguished from gradual, expected operational drift.
Verify that autonomous action triggers include proactive behavior-pattern analysis, security evaluation, and threat-landscape assessment.
Verify that audit logs capture security-critical proactive actions, including approver identity, timestamp, action parameters, and decision outcomes.
Verify that kill-switch activations and override commands are logged.

requirements.section: C12.5 Training Data & Model Lifecycle Audit
requirements.text: Verify that dataset lineage records each dataset and its components, including all transformations, augmentations, and merges.

requirements.section: C12.5 Training Data & Model Lifecycle Audit
requirements.text: Verify that all labeling activities are recorded in logs.

requirements.section: C12.5 Training Data & Model Lifecycle Audit
requirements.text: Verify that all model changes generate immutable audit records.

requirements.section: C12.5 Training Data & Model Lifecycle Audit
requirements.text: Verify that every ingested document is tagged at write time with source, writer identity, and timestamp.
